subject: Post-call recap: SLO targets & sizing for Finex realtime pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T17:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: SLO targets & sizing for Finex realtime pilot

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I loop in ops: 

What we heard (agreed as baseline)
- Primary workload: realtime chat for customer support agents (partial streaming of assistant replies).
- Latency target: end-to-end <= 200 ms p95 (Finex clarified this includes network; they expect ~50–80ms network budget).
- Token/response profile: avg 80 tokens per response, peak bursts up to 600 tokens.
- Expected concurrency: 120–150 concurrent active sessions during peak (mostly 1–2 requests/sec per session).
- Throughput target: ~120–200 req/s sustained, with short bursts to ~350 req/s for 60–120s.

Redwood functional constraints / initial sizing notes
- Streaming is required (partial chunk latency matters). We typically target chunk flushes <= 50 ms for good UX; end-to-end p95 will need careful batching/caching tuning to stay under 200 ms including network.
- Cost levers we discussed: continuous batching (short max latency budget), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, model variant fallback (7B vs 13B), and quantization profiles.

Immediate asks / next steps (please):
1) Alex / Finex: share a 10–30 minute sample of production traces or a synthetic workload file (timestamps, tokens per response, request rates). You mentioned you could export a 24h slice — that would be ideal. Attach to reply or drop in the HubSpot deal.
2) Redwood: we'll produce a short sizing note (ops + cost ballpark) and propose a pilot config (dedicated pool + canary routing + fallback model). Target to share within 24 business hours.
3) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your infra/eng (to align on network budget and test harness). I propose Wed Aug 4 at 09:00 PT — let me know availability.

Attachments referenced: call-recording-20260801.mp4 (recording), workload-sample-aug1.json (empty template we can use).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Date: 2026-08-01T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO targets & sizing for Finex realtime pilot

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the summary. Couple clarifications from our side: 
- Network budget: our infra team measured ~60–80 ms median intra-region latency to Redwood-hosted endpoints; we need to reserve ~80 ms for network to be safe.
- Concurrency: at launch we expect ~150 concurrent agents, but each agent issues 1–3 requests per minute on average — peaks during campaigns could push to 250 concurrent for <10 minutes.
- Streaming: we must support partial responses (token-by-token or chunked streaming). UX requires first chunk within 120 ms of request.
- Budget constraint: target cost for pilot is ~USD 12k–18k/month; if we can show a path to sub-$10k/month at scale with model+quantization levers, procurement will be much happier.

I'll attach a small sample trace (we'll send a 2-hour anonymized trace tomorrow). Also happy to take the Aug 4 meeting — 09:00 PT works for me.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Platform, Finex
alex.carter@finex.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO targets & sizing for Finex realtime pilot — initial sizing + cost levers

Alex / Soojin — quick technical response and a pragmatic set of options to hit the p95 budget while balancing cost. High-level recommendations below; we'll produce a short spreadsheet with numbers (attached).

Targets we mapped to implementation levers
- UX requirement: first chunk <= 120 ms, end-to-end p95 <= 200 ms including ~80 ms network. That leaves ~120 ms compute+queuing for p95.

Option A — Low-latency, higher-cost (Dedicated pool, minimal batching)
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) pinned to 2x A100/RTX-class nodes, single model variant 13B quantized to q4_0 for best perf/accuracy tradeoff.
- Tuning: continuous batching with max batch wait 6–10 ms, streaming chunk flush 40–60 ms. KV prefix caching for templated prompts.
- Expected: p95 compute ~60–90 ms, meets p95 overall; cost: higher (ballpark for pilot USD 16k–22k/mo).

Option B — Cost-optimized, still meeting SLO (hybrid + caching + model variants)
- Deployment: Dedicated with autoscaling + burst to hosted; primary model: 7B finetuned variant (int8/q4 quant), fallback to 13B for long-form responses.
- Tuning: aggressive prefix KV caching (reduces tokens for common assistant openings by ~30–45%), continuous batching with slightly higher max wait 12–20 ms (still meeting UX for most flows), streaming chunk size tuned to prioritize first-chunk latency (send small first chunk quickly).
- Expected: p95 compute ~80–120 ms (combined with network ~180–200 ms); cost: lower, ballpark USD 9k–14k/mo depending on hit rates and cache effectiveness.

Quantization guidance
- Q4_0: good balance, minimal quality regression, strong throughput.
- Int8: best cost reduction but requires careful eval on your prompts — recommend an A/B eval on a sampled prompt set.

Operational and verification items
- We need a 2-hour trace (anonymized) and a representative prompt set to run our eval harness.
- We'll run a 10k-token synthetic canary in our staging to measure first-chunk latency and p95 with your network assumptions.
- Suggested canary window: 48–72 hours with traffic shaping to emulate campaign bursts.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-note.xlsx (contains rough capacity math + ballpark monthly cost per option).

I'll prepare a short one-pager comparing Option A vs B with expected monthly cost ranges and measurable success criteria by tomorrow EOD.

—Rishi
